prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Charlotte after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Charlotte for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but before I give specific firm names it would help to know a couple quick things:
- Do you want a large national firm or a local/smaller boutique trial firm?
- Which part of Charlotte (zip code) or the county where the crash happened?
- Any special facts that matter (catastrophic injury, death, DUI involved, hit-and-run, uninsured motorist, police report)?

If you want me to tailor a short list of actual Charlotte firms to call, tell me the answers above. I can also draft a 30–60 second phone script and a checklist of documents to bring.

While you decide, here’s immediate practical guidance so you can start calling today:

Which specific places to call (now)
- Morgan & Morgan (nationwide with a Charlotte office): large injury firm, contingency-fee, resources for investigations and expert witnesses, often handles serious and complex cases.
- Mecklenburg County Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service: not a firm but will refer you to vetted local personal injury lawyers who handle car-accident cases.
- North Carolina Advocates for Justice (NCAJ) Lawyer Referral: statewide trial lawyer organization; referral will connect you with attorneys experienced in serious injuries and trial work.
- Super Lawyers / Martindale-Hubbell / Avvo / Google Maps listings for “Charlotte personal injury lawyer”: use these to find local solo or boutique firms with high ratings and peer review recognition.

Why these:
- Morgan & Morgan: has resources and staff to handle complex claims, pursue large insurance companies, and fund upfront costs like medical record collection and expert fees.
- Bar association and NCAJ referrals: they connect you to local attorneys who specialize in personal injury and have been screened or are active in the plaintiff bar; good if you want a local attorney with court experience.
- Review sites and peer-rating services: help verify client reviews, peer recognition (Super Lawyers, AV Preeminent ratings), and discipline history.

How to choose between firms when you call
Ask or confirm:
- Do you handle car-accident cases? (Most do, but some focus on other areas.)
- How long have you handled injury trials in Mecklenburg County?
- Do you handle cases on contingency (no fee unless you recover)?
- Who will be my main point of contact — an attorney or a paralegal?
- What percentage is your contingency fee? Any court, filing, or expert costs I’ll be responsible for up front?
- Estimated timeline and whether they do independent medical examinations (IMEs).
- Recent results for similar cases (without guaranteeing outcomes).

What to bring to the first consultation / what to have ready on the call
- Date/time/location of the accident, police report number, names of other drivers and insurers if known
- Photos of the scene, damage, and injuries
- Medical records or notes of treatment so far (ER, ambulance, doctor visits)
- Insurance information (your policy and other driver’s)
- Phone numbers of witnesses, if any
- Paystubs or proof of lost income, if applicable

Important timeline note (North Carolina)
- For most personal-injury claims in NC the statute of limitations is three years from the date of the accident; wrongful-death claims generally have a two-year deadline. Don’t wait to get legal advice if your injuries are significant — missing deadlines can bar your case.

If you want, tell me:
- Your preference (big firm vs local boutique),
- Your zip code or neighborhood,
and I’ll give a short, prioritized list of 4–6 specific Charlotte firms to call plus a phone script you can use.
